Hon'ble Rajesh Singh Chauhan,J.
Heard Ms. Prashansa Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Anand Pratap Singh, learned AGA for the State.

The present applicant is in jail since 22.09.2023, in case crime no. 0029 of 2023, under Sections 333, 353, 354-Kha, 394, 307, 376, 511, 34, 325 and 411 of IPC at Police Station GRP, Ayodhya Cantt,
District Ayodhya/Faizabad.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the present applicant has been falsely implicated and he has not committed any offence as alleged.
Attention has been drawn towards the impugned Vishwambhar Dayal Dubey @ Lallu Tiwari @ ... vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

1 First Information Report, wherein, no specific allegation has been levelled to any one inasmuch as the First Information Report has been lodged against unknown persons.

Attention has been drawn towards annexure no. 2, which is the statement of the victim/injured who is a Police Constable,
wherein, the allegation has been levelled against three unknown persons.
One unknown person was appearing being a middle aged person, aged about 53 to 53 years who tried to snatch the bag of the victim.
The second person had allegedly held the hair of the victim and third person had assaulted upon the victim by a knife or blade and tried to kill the victim.
They also tried to tear the cloths of the victim.
During investigation, the victim was shown the photographs of the person who assaulted the victim through knife or blade and she recognized him as he was the co-accused, namely, Anees.
It has been informed that such accused, Anees has been assassinated in a police encounter.
No identification exercise to identify the present applicant has been carried out and the present applicant has been implicated only on the basis of suspicion.
As per the victim herself, one middle aged person is about 52-53 years, whereas, the present applicant is aged about 45 years.

Ms Prashansa Singh has stated that though the applicant was having no prior criminal history of any kind whatsoever but after the incident in question, when the police tried to arrest the applicant, the applicant allegedly fired upon the Police team, therefore one First Information Report under Section 307 has been registered against him and in that case, the applicant has been granted bail by the Lower Court and the bail order has been annexed as annexure no. 8.

Ms. Prashansa Singh has drawn attention of this Court towards supplementary affidavit, wherein she has annexed the bail rejection order of the present applicant in the same crime case, wherein, Section 325 of IPC was added, therefore, she requested that Section 325 IPC may also be indicated in this order.

Ms.
Prashansa Singh has further submitted that if the victim was able to identify one accused Anees through photographs, he could have identified the present applicant had he been there but the present applicant was not involved in the aforesaid incident, therefore, no exercise of identification of the present applicant has been carried out.
Further, there is no eye witness account or last seen evidence.
The learned counsel has further submitted that if the applicant is released on bail, he shall shall cooperate in the trial proceedings and shall not misuse the liberty of bail.
Further, the applicant shall abide by all terms and conditions of the bail order, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
Learned Additional Government Advocate has, however, opposed the prayer for bail but he has not disputed the aforesaid submission of learned counsel for the applicant.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, perusing the material available on record,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I find it a fit case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant-Vishwambhar Dayal Dubey @ Lallu Tiwari @ Lal Bahadur Dubey, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
Vishwambhar Dayal Dubey @ Lallu Tiwari @ ... vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ...

(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicants fail to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
(v) Before parting with, it is expected that the trial shall be concluded with expedition, strictly in accordance with law, without adjourning the case for any unnecessary reason.

Further, the learned trial court may take all coercive measures,
as per law, if either of the parties do not co-operate in the trial properly.
